sanskrit: ahaṃ ca tat kariṣyāmi yathā kuntīsuto 'rjunaḥ dhārtarāṣṭrasya sainyāni dhakṣyaty agnir ivotthitaḥ
english: And I shall so contrive it that Arjuna, the son of Kuntī, shall burn up the armies of Dhṛtarāṣṭra's son as a blazing fire that has flared up.

sanskrit: adya taṃ pāpakarmāṇaṃ kṣudraṃ saubhadraghātinam apunardarśanaṃ mārgam iṣubhiḥ kṣepsyate 'rjunaḥ
english: This very day Arjuna shall hurl that vile-doing, base slayer of Subhadrā's son down the road from which there is no return.

sanskrit: tasyādya gṛdhrāḥ śyenāś ca vaḍagomāyavas tathā bhakṣayiṣyanti māṃsāni ye cānye puruṣādakāḥ
english: Today vultures and hawks and herons and jackals, and whatever other man-eating creatures there are, shall feast upon his flesh.

sanskrit: yady asya devā goptāraḥ sendrāḥ sarve tathāpy asau rājadhānīṃ yamasyādya hataḥ prāpsyati saṃkule
english: Even if all the gods together with Indra were his protectors, yet this day, slain in the press of battle, he shall reach the royal city of Yama.

sanskrit: nihatya saindhavaṃ jiṣṇur adya tvām upayāsyati viśoko vijvaro rājan bhava bhūtipuraskṛtaḥ
english: Having slain the lord of the Sindhus, the victorious one shall come back to you this very day. Be free of grief and free of fever, O king, and let prosperity attend you.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tathā saṃbhāṣatāṃ teṣāṃ prādurāsīd dhanaṃjayaḥ didṛkṣur bharataśreṣṭhaṃ rājānaṃ sasuhṛdgaṇam
english: Saṃjaya said: As they were thus conversing, Dhanaṃjaya appeared, eager to behold the king, that best of the Bharatas, surrounded by his band of friends.

sanskrit: taṃ praviṣṭaṃ śubhāṃ kakṣyām abhivādyāgrataḥ sthitam samutthāyārjunaṃ premṇā sasvaje pāṇḍavarṣabhaḥ
english: When Arjuna had entered the fair enclosure and, having made obeisance, stood before him, that bull among the Pāṇḍavas rose up and embraced him with love.

sanskrit: mūrdhni cainam upāghrāya pariṣvajya ca bāhunā āśiṣaḥ paramāḥ procya smayamāno 'bhyabhāṣata
english: Kissing him upon the head and folding him in his arms, and pronouncing the highest blessings, he spoke to him, smiling.

sanskrit: vyaktam arjuna saṃgrāme dhruvas te vijayo mahān yādṛg rūpā hi te chāyā prasannaś ca janārdanaḥ
english: Plainly, O Arjuna, your great victory in battle is assured, for such is the radiance of your countenance, and Janārdana is well content.

sanskrit: tam abravīt tato jiṣṇur mahad āścaryam uttamam dṛṣṭavān asmi bhadraṃ te keśavasya prasādajam
english: Then the victorious one answered him: I have beheld a great and surpassing marvel, born of the grace of Keśava—blessings be upon you.

sanskrit: tatas tat kathayām āsa yathādṛṣṭaṃ dhanaṃjayaḥ āśvāsanārthaṃ suhṛdāṃ tryambakena samāgamam
english: Then Dhanaṃjaya, to hearten his friends, related as he had witnessed it his meeting with the three-eyed god.

sanskrit: tataḥ śirobhir avaniṃ spṛṣṭvā sarve ca vismitāḥ namaskṛtya vṛṣāṅkāya sādhu sādhv ity athābruvan
english: Then all of them, wonder-struck, touched the earth with their heads, and bowing to the god whose emblem is the bull, cried, "Well done, well done!"

sanskrit: anujñātās tataḥ sarve suhṛdo dharmasūnunā tvaramāṇāḥ susaṃnaddhā hṛṣṭā yuddhāya niryayuḥ
english: Then all the friends, given leave by the son of Dharma, well girt and full of gladness, hastened forth to battle.

sanskrit: abhivādya tu rājānaṃ yuyudhānācyutārjunāḥ hṛṣṭā viniryayus te vai yudhiṣṭhiraniveśanāt
english: Having saluted the king, Yuyudhāna, Acyuta, and Arjuna went forth rejoicing from the dwelling of Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: rathenaikena durdharṣau yuyudhānajanārdanau jagmatuḥ sahitau vīrāv arjunasya niveśanam
english: On a single chariot the unassailable heroes Yuyudhāna and Janārdana went together to the encampment of Arjuna.

sanskrit: tatra gatvā hṛṣīkeśaḥ kalpayām āsa sūtavat rathaṃ rathavarasyājau vānararṣabhalakṣaṇam
english: Having gone there, Hṛṣīkeśa, like a charioteer, made ready for the foremost of chariot-warriors that battle-car which bore the ensign of the bull-like ape.

sanskrit: sa meghasamanirghoṣas taptakāñcanasaprabhaḥ babhau rathavaraḥ kḷptaḥ śiśur divasakṛd yathā
english: That noble chariot, roaring like a thundercloud and gleaming with the splendor of refined gold, when made ready shone like the newborn sun.

sanskrit: tataḥ puruṣaśārdūlaḥ sajjaḥ sajjaṃ puraḥsaraḥ kṛtāhnikāya pārthāya nyavedayata taṃ ratham
english: Then that tiger among men, himself accoutred, going before, presented the equipped chariot to Pārtha, who had performed his daily rites.

sanskrit: taṃ tu loke varaḥ puṃsāṃ kirīṭī hemavarmabhṛt bāṇabāṇāsanī vāhaṃ pradakṣiṇam avartata
english: And the Diademed One, the best of men in the world, clad in golden mail and bearing his bow and arrows, walked round that vehicle in reverent circuit.

sanskrit: tato vidyāvayovṛddhaiḥ kriyāvadbhir jitendriyaiḥ stūyamāno jayāśībhir āruroha mahāratham
english: Then, hymned with blessings of victory by men ripe in learning and in years, given to holy rites and masters of their senses, he mounted the great chariot.

sanskrit: jaitraiḥ sāṃgrāmikair mantraiḥ pūrvam eva rathottamam abhimantritam arciṣmān udayaṃ bhāskaro yathā
english: That best of chariots had already been consecrated with martial, victory-bringing spells, and the radiant hero mounted it as the rising sun mounts the horizon.

sanskrit: sa rathe rathināṃ śreṣṭhaḥ kāñcane kāñcanāvṛtaḥ vibabhau vimalo 'rciṣmān merāv iva divākaraḥ
english: That foremost of car-warriors, clad in gold, upon his golden chariot shone spotless and radiant, like the sun upon Mount Meru.

sanskrit: anvārurohatuḥ pārthaṃ yuyudhānajanārdanau śaryāter yajñam āyāntaṃ yathendraṃ devam aśvinau
english: Yuyudhāna and Janārdana mounted up after Pārtha, as the two Aśvins follow the god Indra when he comes to the sacrifice of Śaryāti.

sanskrit: atha jagrāha govindo raśmīn raśmivatāṃ varaḥ mātalir vāsavasyeva vṛtraṃ hantuṃ prayāsyataḥ
english: Then Govinda, best of those who hold the reins, took up the reins, as Mātali did for Vāsava when he set forth to slay Vṛtra.

sanskrit: sa tābhyāṃ sahitaḥ pārtho rathapravaram āsthitaḥ sahito budhaśukrābhyāṃ tamo nighnan yathā śaśī
english: Pārtha, mounted upon that noblest of chariots together with those two, was like the moon flanked by Mercury and Venus, dispelling the darkness.

sanskrit: saindhavasya vadhaprepsuḥ prayātaḥ śatrupūgahā sahāmbupatimitrābhyāṃ yathendras tārakāmaye
english: Eager to slay the lord of the Sindhus, that destroyer of throngs of foes set forth, like Indra in the war against Tāraka, accompanied by Varuṇa, lord of waters, and by Mitra.

sanskrit: tato vāditranirghoṣair maṅgalyaiś ca stavaiḥ śubhaiḥ prayāntam arjunaṃ sūtā māgadhāś caiva tuṣṭuvuḥ
english: Then, as Arjuna went forth, bards and panegyrists praised him with the sound of instruments and with auspicious, holy hymns.

sanskrit: sajayāśīḥ sapuṇyāhaḥ sūtamāgadhanisvanaḥ yukto vāditraghoṣeṇa teṣāṃ ratikaro 'bhavat
english: That sound of bards and minstrels, attended with blessings of victory and with proclamations of the holy day, joined to the music of instruments, became to them a thing of delight.

sanskrit: tam anuprayato vāyuḥ puṇyagandhavahaḥ śuciḥ vavau saṃharṣayan pārthaṃ dviṣataś cāpi śoṣayan
english: A pure breeze, bearing holy fragrances, blew gently after him, gladdening Pārtha and withering his foes.

sanskrit: prādurāsan nimittāni vijayāya bahūni ca pāṇḍavānāṃ tvadīyānāṃ viparītāni māriṣa
english: Many omens appeared, foretelling victory for the Pāṇḍavas and, for your men, the contrary, O venerable one.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvārjuno nimittāni vijayāya pradakṣiṇam yuyudhānaṃ maheṣvāsam idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Seeing the favorable omens of victory, Arjuna spoke these words to Yuyudhāna, the mighty archer.

sanskrit: yuyudhānādya yuddhe me dṛśyate vijayo dhruvaḥ yathā hīmāni liṅgāni dṛśyante śinipuṃgava
english: O Yuyudhāna, this day my victory in battle is plainly assured, for such are the signs that appear, O bull of Śini's line.

sanskrit: so 'haṃ tatra gamiṣyāmi yatra saindhavako nṛpaḥ yiyāsur yamalokāya mama vīryaṃ pratīkṣate
english: I shall go thither, where the king of the Sindhus, ready to depart for the realm of Yama, awaits my prowess.

sanskrit: yathā paramakaṃ kṛtyaṃ saindhavasya vadhe mama tathaiva sumahat kṛtyaṃ dharmarājasya rakṣaṇe
english: As the slaying of the lord of the Sindhus is my highest task, even so is the guarding of the king of righteousness a most weighty task.

sanskrit: sa tvam adya mahābāho rājānaṃ paripālaya yathaiva hi mayā guptas tvayā gupto bhavet tathā
english: Therefore do you this day, O mighty-armed one, guard the king, so that he may be as well protected by you as he would be by me.

sanskrit: tvayi cāhaṃ parāśvasya pradyumne vā mahārathe śaknuyāṃ saindhavaṃ hantum anapekṣo nararṣabha
english: Trusting in you, or in Pradyumna that great car-warrior, I shall be able to slay the lord of the Sindhus free of all anxiety, O bull among men.

sanskrit: mayy apekṣā na kartavyā kathaṃ cid api sātvata rājany eva parā guptiḥ kāryā sarvātmanā tvayā
english: No concern need you have on my account in any way, O Sātvata; the king is your supreme charge, to be guarded by you with all your soul.

sanskrit: na hi yatra mahābāhur vāsudevo vyavasthitaḥ kiṃ cid vyāpadyate tatra yatrāham api ca dhruvam
english: For where the mighty-armed Vāsudeva stands fixed, and where I am as well, there no harm can ever befall—of that be sure.

sanskrit: evam uktas tu pārthena sātyakiḥ paravīrahā tathety uktvāgamat tatra yatra rājā yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: Thus addressed by Pārtha, Sātyaki, slayer of hostile heroes, said, "So be it," and went thither where King Yudhiṣṭhira was.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca śvobhūte kim akārṣus te duḥkhaśokasamanvitāḥ abhimanyau hate tatra ke vāyudhyanta māmakāḥ
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: When the next day came, what did they do, beset with grief and sorrow? When Abhimanyu had been slain there, which of my men gave battle?

sanskrit: jānantas tasya karmāṇi kuravaḥ savyasācinaḥ kathaṃ tat kilbiṣaṃ kṛtvā nirbhayā brūhi māmakāḥ
english: Knowing the deeds of Savyasācin, how could my Kurus, having wrought that sin, remain unafraid? Tell me.

sanskrit: putraśokābhisaṃtaptaṃ kruddhaṃ mṛtyum ivāntakam āyāntaṃ puruṣavyāghraṃ kathaṃ dadṛśur āhave
english: How did they look upon that tiger among men in battle as he came on, scorched with grief for his son and wrathful as death the ender?

sanskrit: kapirājadhvajaṃ saṃkhye vidhunvānaṃ mahad dhanuḥ dṛṣṭvā putraparidyūnaṃ kim akurvanta māmakāḥ
english: Seeing in the fray the bearer of the ape-king ensign, brandishing his mighty bow and stricken with grief for his son, what did my men do?

sanskrit: kiṃ nu saṃjaya saṃgrāme vṛttaṃ duryodhanaṃ prati paridevo mahān atra śruto me nābhinandanam
english: What befell Duryodhana in the battle, O Saṃjaya? Here I hear only great lamentation, and no word of rejoicing.

sanskrit: babhūvur ye manogrāhyāḥ śabdāḥ śrutisukhāvahāḥ na śrūyante 'dya te sarve saindhavasya niveśane
english: Those sounds that once charmed the mind and brought delight to the ear are none of them heard this day in the encampment of the lord of the Sindhus.

sanskrit: stuvatāṃ nādya śrūyante putrāṇāṃ śibire mama sūtamāgadhasaṃghānāṃ nartakānāṃ ca sarvaśaḥ
english: In the camp of my sons no longer are heard, anywhere, the voices of the throngs of bards and panegyrists and dancers raised in praise.

sanskrit: śabdena nāditābhīkṣṇam abhavad yatra me śrutiḥ dīnānām adya taṃ śabdaṃ na śṛṇomi samīritam
english: Where once my ears were filled unceasingly with their sounds, today I no longer hear that sound raised up by men now sunk in misery.

sanskrit: niveśane satyadhṛteḥ somadattasya saṃjaya āsīno 'haṃ purā tāta śabdam aśrauṣam uttamam
english: In the dwelling of Somadatta of steadfast vow, O Saṃjaya, as I sat there once before, my son, I used to hear a most excellent sound.

sanskrit: tad adya hīnapuṇyo 'ham ārtasvaranināditam niveśanaṃ hatotsāhaṃ putrāṇāṃ mama lakṣaye
english: But today, stripped of my merit, I mark the dwelling of my sons resounding with cries of anguish, its spirit broken.

sanskrit: viviṃśater durmukhasya citrasenavikarṇayoḥ anyeṣāṃ ca sutānāṃ me na tathā śrūyate dhvaniḥ
english: From Viviṃśati, from Durmukha, from Citrasena and Vikarṇa, and from my other sons, no such sound is heard as before.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇāḥ kṣatriyā vaiśyā yaṃ śiṣyāḥ paryupāsate droṇaputraṃ maheṣvāsaṃ putrāṇāṃ me parāyaṇam
english: Around the son of Droṇa, the mighty archer, the refuge of my sons, brāhmaṇas, kṣatriyas, vaiśyas, and pupils used to gather in attendance—

sanskrit: vitaṇḍālāpasaṃlāpair hutayācitavanditaiḥ gītaiś ca vividhair iṣṭai ramate yo divāniśam
english: he who delights day and night in disputations and discourses and conversations, in oblations, in petitions and praises, and in songs of many cherished kinds—

sanskrit: upāsyamāno bahubhiḥ kurupāṇḍavasātvataiḥ sūta tasya gṛhe śabdho nādya drauṇer yathā purā
english: attended by many of the Kurus, Pāṇḍavas, and Sātvatas—O bard, in the abode of that son of Droṇa there is today no such sound as before.

sanskrit: droṇaputraṃ maheṣvāsaṃ gāyanā nartakāś ca ye atyartham upatiṣṭhanti teṣāṃ na śrūyate dhvaniḥ
english: The singers and dancers who used to wait in great numbers upon the son of Droṇa, that mighty archer—their voices are no longer heard.

sanskrit: vindānuvindayoḥ sāyaṃ śibire yo mahādhvaniḥ śrūyate so 'dya na tathā kekayānāṃ ca veśmasu
english: That great clamor that of an evening was heard in the camp of Vinda and Anuvinda, and in the dwellings of the Kekayas, is not so heard today.

sanskrit: nityapramuditānāṃ ca tālagītasvano mahān nṛtyatāṃ śrūyate tāta gaṇānāṃ so 'dya na dhvaniḥ
english: And that great sound of cymbals and song from the ever-merry companies as they danced—that din, my son, is not heard today.

sanskrit: saptatantūn vitanvānā yam upāsanti yājakāḥ saumadattiṃ śrutanidhiṃ teṣāṃ na śrūyate dhvaniḥ
english: The officiating priests who, spreading out the seven-threaded sacrifice, used to wait upon Somadatta's son, that treasury of sacred lore—their voices are not heard.

sanskrit: jyāghoṣo brahmaghoṣaś ca tomarāsirathadhvaniḥ droṇasyāsīd avirato gṛhe tan na śṛṇomy aham
english: The twang of bowstrings, the chanting of the Vedas, the clatter of lances and swords and chariots that sounded ceaselessly in the abode of Droṇa—that I no longer hear.

sanskrit: nānādeśasamutthānāṃ gītānāṃ yo 'bhavat svanaḥ vāditranāditānāṃ ca so 'dya na śrūyate mahān
english: That great sound of songs arising from many lands, and of instruments resounding, is not heard today.

sanskrit: yadā prabhṛty upaplavyāc chāntim icchañ janārdanaḥ āgataḥ sarvabhūtānām anukampārtham acyutaḥ
english: From the time that Janārdana, the imperishable one, came from Upaplavya, desiring peace out of compassion for all beings—

sanskrit: tato 'ham abruvaṃ sūta mandaṃ duryodhanaṃ tadā vāsudevena tīrthena putra saṃśāmya pāṇḍavaiḥ
english: then, O bard, I said to the foolish Duryodhana: "Through Vāsudeva as your worthy mediator, my son, make peace with the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: kālaprāptam ahaṃ manye mā tvaṃ duryodhanātigāḥ śame ced yācamānaṃ tvaṃ pratyākhyāsyasi keśavam hitārtham abhijalpantaṃ na tathāsty aparājayaḥ
english: I think this fitted to the hour. Do not, O Duryodhana, overstep the bounds. If you reject Keśava when he sues for peace and speaks for your good, then there can be no victory for you."

sanskrit: pratyācaṣṭa sa dāśārham ṛṣabhaṃ sarvadhanvinām anuneyāni jalpantam anayān nānvapadyata
english: But he rebuffed that bull of the Dāśārhas, the foremost of all bowmen, as he spoke words deserving of compliance, and out of waywardness he would not yield.

sanskrit: tato duḥśāsanasyaiva karṇasya ca mataṃ dvayoḥ anvavartata hitvā māṃ kṛṣṭaḥ kālena durmatiḥ
english: Then, forsaking me, that evil-minded one, dragged on by Fate, followed the counsel of those two, Duḥśāsana and Karṇa.

sanskrit: na hy ahaṃ dyūtam icchāmi viduro na praśaṃsati saindhavo necchate dyūtaṃ bhīṣmo na dyūtam icchati
english: For I myself did not desire the gambling; Vidura did not approve it; the lord of the Sindhus did not wish for the game; Bhīṣma did not wish for the game;

sanskrit: śalyo bhūriśravāś caiva purumitro jayas tathā aśvatthāmā kṛpo droṇo dyūtaṃ necchanti saṃjaya
english: Śalya and Bhūriśravas, Purumitra and Jaya, Aśvatthāman, Kṛpa, and Droṇa—none of them desired the game, O Saṃjaya.

sanskrit: eteṣāṃ matam ājñāya yadi varteta putrakaḥ sajñātimitraḥ sasuhṛc ciraṃ jīved anāmayaḥ
english: Had my boy but known the mind of these and acted upon it, he, with his kinsmen and his allies and his friends, would have lived long and free of affliction.

sanskrit: ślakṣṇā madhurasaṃbhāṣā jñātimadhye priyaṃvadāḥ kulīnāḥ saṃmatāḥ prājñāḥ sukhaṃ prāpsyanti pāṇḍavāḥ
english: Gentle, sweet of speech, kindly-spoken among their kin, well-born, honored, and wise, the Pāṇḍavas shall surely attain happiness.

sanskrit: dharmāpekṣo naro nityaṃ sarvatra labhate sukham pretyabhāve ca kalyāṇaṃ prasādaṃ pratipadyate
english: The man who ever has regard for righteousness gains happiness everywhere, and in the world to come attains blessedness and grace.

sanskrit: arhanty ardhaṃ pṛthivyās te bhoktuṃ sāmarthyasādhanāḥ teṣām api samudrāntā pitṛpaitāmahī mahī
english: They, possessed of power and resource, deserve to enjoy half the earth; and theirs too is the sea-girt land, inherited from their fathers and forefathers.

sanskrit: niyujyamānāḥ sthāsyanti pāṇḍavā dharmavartmani santi no jñātayas tāta yeṣāṃ śroṣyanti pāṇḍavāḥ
english: If so directed, the Pāṇḍavas will keep to the path of righteousness; and we have kinsmen, my son, to whom the Pāṇḍavas will hearken—

sanskrit: śalyasya somadattasya bhīṣmasya ca mahātmanaḥ droṇasyātha vikarṇasya bāhlikasya kṛpasya ca
english: to Śalya, to Somadatta, to the great-souled Bhīṣma, to Droṇa and Vikarṇa, to Bāhlika and Kṛpa,

sanskrit: anyeṣāṃ caiva vṛddhānāṃ bharatānāṃ mahātmanām tvadarthaṃ bruvatāṃ tāta kariṣyanti vaco hitam
english: and to the other aged, great-souled Bharatas; when these speak for your good, my son, the Pāṇḍavas will heed their wholesome word.

sanskrit: kaṃ vā tvaṃ manyase teṣāṃ yas tvā brūyād ato 'nyathā kṛṣṇo na dharmaṃ saṃjahyāt sarve te ca tvadanvayāḥ
english: Which of them do you suppose would counsel you otherwise than this? Kṛṣṇa would not abandon righteousness, and all those others follow your lead.

sanskrit: mayāpi coktās te vīrā vacanaṃ dharmasaṃhitam nānyathā prakariṣyanti dharmātmāno hi pāṇḍavāḥ
english: I too have spoken to those heroes a word in keeping with righteousness; they will not act otherwise, for the Pāṇḍavas are devoted to dharma.

sanskrit: ity ahaṃ vilapan sūta bahuśaḥ putram uktavān na ca me śrutavān mūḍho manye kālasya paryayam
english: Thus, O bard, lamenting, I spoke to my son again and again; yet the fool would not heed me. I deem it the turning of the wheel of Time.

sanskrit: vṛkodarārjunau yatra vṛṣṇivīraś ca sātyakiḥ uttamaujāś ca pāñcālyo yudhāmanyuś ca durjayaḥ
english: Where Vṛkodara and Arjuna are, and Sātyaki, the Vṛṣṇi hero, and Uttamaujas the Pāñcāla, and Yudhāmanyu hard to conquer,

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭadyumnaś ca durdharṣaḥ śikhaṇḍī cāparājitaḥ aśmakāḥ kekayāś caiva kṣatradharmā ca saumakiḥ
english: and the unassailable Dhṛṣṭadyumna, and the unvanquished Śikhaṇḍin, the Aśmakas and the Kekayas, and Kṣatradharman the son of the Somakas,

sanskrit: caidyaś ca cekitānaś ca putraḥ kāśyasya cābhibhuḥ draupadeyā virāṭaś ca drupadaś ca mahārathaḥ yamau ca puruṣavyāghrau mantrī ca madhusūdanaḥ
english: and the Caidya and Cekitāna, and Abhibhū the son of the king of Kāśi, the sons of Draupadī, Virāṭa and Drupada that great car-warrior, the twins, those tigers among men, and the slayer of Madhu for counselor—

sanskrit: ka etāñ jātu yudhyeta loke 'smin vai jijīviṣuḥ divyam astraṃ vikurvāṇān saṃhareyur ariṃdamāḥ
english: who in this world that wished to live would ever do battle with these subduers of foes, who wield and let loose the celestial weapons?
